Nvidia staff: what do you think of Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive?

One can imagine high-fives all around Nvidia’s boardroom after the board reinstated Jensen Huang to the CEO suite. The market gave the move a fat thumbs-up, boosting Nvidia’s share price by about a third. Shareholders, whose interests the board is meant to represent, are surely happy.
But like Fifa’s controversial decision to defer the one-match suspension of US forward Folarin Balogun after receiving a red card for a foul on Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Tarik Muharemović during the World Cup over the summer, Huang’s absolution might backfire.
Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletter Being There on Substack

articles.title: GTA VI’s jaw-dropping success: in figures
articles.summary:
Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch
Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know.
Data on streaming the game suggests that only two days into its release a cumulative 364.5m hours have been watched – roughly 41,000 years of content. Put another way, that translates to more than 41,000 years worth of people riffling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving or hijacking jets. That’s according to streaming data from Streams Charts, a data and analytics company that has been tracking Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title.

Man Theft Auto – why did so few women review GTA VI, the biggest video game of the decade?
articles.summary:
Given that this is the first Grand Theft Auto in 30 years with a female protagonist, you might have expected to hear from female critics. But you would have expected mostly in vain
Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch of all time, and is likely to become the biggest video game of all time. It’s a once-in-a-lifetime event, a phenomenon that will shape games as a medium and pop culture at large for years to come, set against the backdrop of its developers fighting for their rights at studio Rockstar Games. It has snatched sales and streaming records and become the best-reviewed game ever (pulling ahead of 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time). It’s also the first GTA game with a female protagonist, who also happens to be a woman of colour. Yet very few women (and seemingly no women of colour) played and reviewed it before release.
When GTA VI’s review embargo lifted on 18 November, the gender imbalance was immediately obvious. Out of 156 reviewers, only six appeared to be women. As journalist Lex Luddy noted in a BlueSky post, that is 3.8%.

articles.title: Hacking radiators
The unexpected joy hiding in Grand Theft Auto VI’s chaos? A little routine
articles.summary:
Rockstar’s latest blockbuster makes the everyday business of shopping, working out and taking care of a pet snake as compelling as its shootouts and car chases
I knew I’d need many skills during the opening hours of Grand Theft Auto VI, but effective time management was not one of them. From playing the previous five titles in the series (and their many spin-offs), I understood I’d have to master Rockstar’s idiosyncratic approach to car handling. True enough, the vehicles do drive like airbeds tied on top of supermarket trolleys. I also knew I’d need to get to grips with the somewhat tricky aiming and shooting if I was to commit any sort of respectable crime spree.
But for the first few hours of playing this staggeringly large and bewildering game, what concerned me most was lead character Jason’s personal routine. Each day, he needs to get up, choose an outfit, complete a workout, feed his pet snake Dolores, and perhaps do some DIY, so that when his girlfriend Lucia gets out of jail she’ll fall for him again – rather than fall through his apartment’s rotten staircase. Meanwhile, his drug-smuggling boss phones every five minutes with new parcels for Jason to pick up or drop off, and his pals Cal and Donnie get into all sorts of cocaine-related hijinks they expect Jason to extricate them from. There are also predatory neighbours to do favours for, and groceries to buy. I’ve seen so many people on social media posting about how they took several days off work to play this game, only to find themselves busier and more productive than ever. On his radio show last week, James O’Brien derided himself for completing, in Jason’s apartment, a simple DIY task that he’s put off for months in his own home. I know where he’s coming from.
